title: Port a verified SQL analyst from Fireworks to Crusoe

input.records: 0..500 JSON objects. Each has repo, owner, stars, forks, issues, license, description, url. Strings except stars/forks/issues which are nonnegative integers <= 2^53-1. license and description may be null. Missing or extra fields are invalid. Bool is not an integer. String length <= 4000.
input.sql: A nonempty string <=4096 characters. Exactly one read-only SQLite SELECT or WITH query. Comments and literal words such as DROP are allowed. No arbitrary paths or database identifiers.

behavior: Build an in-memory SQLite table named repositories with the eight declared columns, using parameterized inserts.
Execute the requested SELECT query with SQLite semantics. Return {columns:[names],rows:[[values]]}. Preserve order, null, zero, Unicode and duplicate rows.
Use SQLite authorizer/query-only controls after initialization. Deny writes, DDL, PRAGMA, ATTACH, DETACH, extension loading, file functions and transactions. Do not rely on a keyword blacklist.
Limit result rows to 100 and columns to 20. Abort expensive queries with a SQLite progress handler.
Never access the network, disk files, subprocesses or dynamic Python internals. sqlite3.connect must use :memory:. Allowed imports: sqlite3,json,re,typing,collections,math.

Return {error:code} without raw exceptions. Codes: invalid_request for malformed payload, query_error for syntax/missing table/column, read_only for denied SQL operations, limit_exceeded for oversized payload/results or interrupted expensive queries.
scope: Port the schema/query/result-set workflow, not Fireworks GRPO training or its Chroma retriever. The target uses Crusoe inference with fixed model weights.
